input.args: Issue 340: Scala trait with a concrete method, mocked with Mockito.mock(classOf[Trait], CALLS_REAL_METHODS). Calling getTrue returns false instead of calling the real method (true). Evidence: mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/internal/stubbing/answers/CallsRealMethods.java returns RETURNS_DEFAULTS when Modifier.isAbstract(method) is true; mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/Answers.java defines CALLS_REAL_METHODS. Likely cause: Scala 2.11 compiles trait concrete methods to an abstract interface method plus a $class helper, so the method looks abstract to Mockito.

final: {"number": 340, "label": "bug", "route": "repro-check", "related": [2818, 2620, 146], "evidence": ["mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/internal/stubbing/answers/CallsRealMethods.java", "mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/Answers.java"], "reply": "Thanks for the report. The snippet plus the expected (true) and actual (false) results are enough to reproduce this as written. The behaviour lives in CallsRealMethods (org.mockito.internal.stubbing.answers), which falls back to the default answer whenever the invoked method is abstract, so a trait method that the compiler emits as abstract never reaches the real implementation."}
